llm.summary: The skill's declared requirements and instructions line up with its stated purpose (scraping and analyzing e‑commerce reviews), but it relies on browser automation with logged‑in sessions and runtime package installation — which require cautious use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (analyzing Taobao/JD/Pinduoduo reviews) matches the requested artifacts: python3, a Chinese text segmentation dependency (jieba), and a browser automation workflow. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to perform browser automation and requires the user to be logged into the target platforms; the provided Python analysis code only processes review text and does not exfiltrate data. However the instructions are high‑level and do not explicitly limit scraping to review pages or specify how extracted data is handled, so browser automation could potentially access other data in the logged‑in session unless constrained by the platform.

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction‑only). The SKILL.md suggests 'pip install jieba' which is a normal PyPI dependency for Chinese text processing. There are no downloads from unknown URLs or archive extraction instructions.

Still, it requires access to a logged‑in browser session for scraping — that implicitly uses session cookies/credentials stored in the user's browser. The skill does not declare or document how those session artifacts will be used or protected.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims (scrape and analyze reviews) and requests only python and a Chinese NLP library. Before installing or running it: (1) prefer running it with a test account or in a sandboxed browser profile to avoid exposing unrelated account data (messages, orders, payment info) from your main logged‑in session; (2) review any runtime steps that enable browser automation to confirm it only visits/retrieves review pages; (3) be aware that 'pip install jieba' will fetch packages from PyPI — only proceed if you trust that dependency; (4) avoid supplying external credentials via environment variables (none are required) and inspect any output destinations to ensure reviews are not transmitted to unknown endpoints. If you need higher assurance, request a version that includes explicit browser‑scoping rules and a clear data handling policy or provide a local export of reviews rather than giving the skill access to your logged‑in session.
